newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium market absorbs rising stocks trend.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium market absorbs rising stocks trend.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium stocks rose by a net 9,875 tonnes this week, but a backdrop of steady demand and tight nearby backwardations neant the market managed to absorb the builds, traders said in Friday.
Zinc stocks fell by 12,225 tonnes, while copper inventories in the traditionally slow summer period rose by 12,175 tonnes.
Total aluminium stocks stand at 631,850 tonnes following four consecutive gains, but remain down 32.4 percent, or 303,225 tonnes, on the year to date.

Traders expected further gains next week. "The increase in stocks in Japan has been attributed to Korean deliveries where traders have reported that demand has eased significantly in recent weeks," Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said.
"Whilst currently monitoring the stock rise we feel they are of little concern at least until a couple of weeks of increases have been posted," Squires added.
"Unless a flood of metal is delivered onto the LME over the next few weeks then the prospects for aluminium seems good," brokers GNI said.
During Friday morning trading three months aluminium prices held steady at around $1,700 a tonne. Traders said the market was finding support from tight nearby backwardations.
"There is a feeling that August long positions are being rolled over to November, which offers the prospect of tightness through to the end of the year," GNI said.
On the week zinc inventories fell by 12,225 tonnes. Year to date total inventories have fallen by 114,875 tonnes, or 22.9 percent.

Nearby tightness is also supporting zinc. "The fundamentals continue to support the market's strength, with stocks in decline and the widening of the backwardation within the spread, reflecting the nearby market tightness," Squires of Wolff said.
During the past week copper stocks rose by 12,175 tonnes.
"A continued rise in stocks should outweigh any support the market may derive from short covering against next week's August date," LME brokers Brandeis said.
"Copper inventory additions both in LME and Comex warehouses have further pressured the copper price," Flemings Global Mining Group said.
Traders said copper stocks would continue to arrive during the summer period, a condition that has seen tight nearby backwardations contract.
"The once huge backwardation which earlier this year blew out to $300 a tonne has wilted and shrivelled away to less than $10 a tonne," Flemings noted.

Despite a strike at Canada's Falconbridge, nickel stocks rose by 2,412 tonnes during the week. "While supplies of both primary nickel and nickel contained in scrap are strong at a time of seasonally slow demand...evidence of the weak fundamentals are reflected in the rise of LME stocks," Brandeis said.
